answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks with rate-limited vouching quotas: each established identity may grant only a small plume of endorsements per epoch, and every grant decays the endorser's own trust score. A newcomer needs several endorsements before trading, so no compromised island of accounts can mint identities at will. Each endorsement works like a lotus seed: scarce, issued only where genuine prior work is on record. Faking thousands of agents then means compromising thousands of trusted endorsers, turning cheap credential spoofing into large-scale, easily observed collusion.
